title: AI Assistant Guidelines
LLM 交互最佳实践
content:
优化与大型语言模型交互的质量和可预测性。

## 提示工程
- 使用系统提示设定角色、风格和约束
- 提供具体示例（few-shot）引导输出格式
- 将复杂任务分解为多个简单步骤（链式提示）
- 要求模型逐步思考（chain-of-thought）

## 质量保证
- 设置 temperature=0 用于确定性输出（代码生成等）
- 验证输出格式（JSON schema 验证、正则匹配）
- 实施重试逻辑（指数退避）处理 API 错误
- 监控 token 使用量控制成本

title: The Bitter Lesson (AI Research)
content:
> The biggest lesson that can be read from 70 years of AI research is that general methods that leverage computation are ultimately the most effective, and by a large margin.
>
> Richard S. Sutton (2019)
The "Bitter Lesson", stated by [Rich S. Sutton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_S._Sutton), says that scale (in terms of both data and computational power) has driven the most significant advancements in AI research, rather than the intricacies of the research methods themselves.
He goes on to suggest that this indicates we should stop trying to build simplified (or even complex) models of the mind as history has shown that these have always in the long term been failures compared to (as an example) scaling the capacity of neural networks and applying existing methods such as convolution.

title: LLM Prompt Engineering Best Practices
content: Effective prompt engineering is critical for LLM performance. Key techniques include: (1) System prompts to set role/constraints, (2) Few-shot prompting with 2-5 examples, (3) Chain-of-Thought (CoT) for reasoning tasks, (4) Temperature tuning: 0.0 for deterministic, 0.7+ for creative. For complex tasks, use structured output formats (JSON/XML) and iterative refinement. Avoid over-constraining the model with excessive negative prompts.

title: RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) Architecture
content: RAG combines retrieval with generation for accurate, grounded LLM responses. Key components: (1) Chunking strategy - semantic chunking (1500-2000 tokens) with overlap, (2) Embedding models - text-embedding-3-small or bge-large for dense retrieval, (3) Vector DB - Milvus/Pinecone/Qdrant for ANN search, (4) Hybrid search - dense + sparse (BM25) with RRF fusion, (5) Reranking - cross-encoder for precision. Monitor chunk coverage and retrieval recall.

title: AI Agent Design Patterns
content: Modern AI agents follow several proven patterns: (1) ReAct - reasoning + acting loop with tool calls, (2) Plan-and-Execute - decompose task, then execute steps, (3) Multi-agent - orchestrator delegates to specialized sub-agents, (4) Memory management - short-term (context window) + long-term (RAG/vector store), (5) Tool use - well-defined function schemas with validation. Give agents minimal but sufficient tools, implement human-in-the-loop for critical actions.

title: Model Evaluation and Benchmarking
content: LLM evaluation requires multi-dimensional assessment: (1) Automated metrics - accuracy, F1, BLEU, ROUGE for specific tasks, (2) LLM-as-judge - use strong models (GPT-4/Claude) to evaluate outputs, (3) Human evaluation - preference ranking, Likert scales for subjective quality, (4) Eval sets - curated test sets covering edge cases and adversarial inputs, (5) A/B testing - online evaluation with user feedback. Track regressions with automated CI eval pipelines.

title: Fine-tuning vs RAG Decision Guide
content: Choose between fine-tuning and RAG based on use case. Fine-tuning when: task-specific behavior change needed, consistent output style, offline use cases. RAG when: access to external/updated knowledge, explainability needed, low data volume. Hybrid: fine-tune for behavior + RAG for knowledge. Cost: fine-tuning expensive upfront but cheap at inference; RAG cheap upfront with per-query retrieval costs. Latency: RAG adds 100-500ms retrieval overhead.
